The results were, indeed, better than anyone had expected.
diverged: The two rivers diverged after flowing together for several miles.
recent: happening or made a short time ago
Her most recent film received excellent reviews from critics.
decades: The old bridge has stood for decades without major repairs.
ways: It is one of the clearest ways in which a city changes the weather.
still: continuing to be the case; even more so
Despite the rain, the match still went ahead as planned.
fully: The patient has fully recovered from the surgery.
explained: made clear by being described in detail
A few proxies have diverged from what the model explained before.
happens: takes place; occurs, third person singular
It happens more often than people realise during exam season.
affected: Families affected by the flood received emergency housing support.
flagged: marked as needing attention or being unusual
The system flagged several transactions as suspicious.
exclude: to leave something or someone out; to not include
Reconstructions that exclude flagged records are published alongside the full ones.
published: prepared and issued for the public to read
Her first novel was published when she was only twenty-two.
alongside: next to or together with something else
The new bike lane runs alongside the main road through downtown.
those: used to refer to people or things further away or already mentioned
Those houses on the hill were built a century ago.
conclusions: judgments reached after considering all the facts
The two studies drew very different conclusions from similar data.
far: to a great extent; at or to a great distance
This plan works far better than the last one did.
turned: past tense of turn; changed direction or became something different
Both guesses turned out to be backwards.
choice: an act of selecting between two or more possibilities
Choosing a university was a difficult choice for her.
made: The table was made entirely from reclaimed wood.
fact: a thing that is known to be true
It is a fact that the Earth orbits the Sun.
openly: in a way that is not hidden or secret; honestly
She spoke openly about the challenges she faced at work.
itself: used to refer back to a thing or situation already mentioned, for emphasis
The machine can clean itself without any help from a technician.
part: a piece or portion of a whole
Only a small part of the report dealt with financial risks.
makes: A short walk after dinner makes falling asleep much easier.
field: an area of open land, often used for crops or animals
The farmer ploughed the field before planting corn.
credible: able to be trusted or believed
The witness gave a credible account of what happened at the scene.
emerges: comes out or becomes visible after being hidden
A new leader usually emerges once the old system fails.
picture: an image, painting, drawing, or photograph
He hung a picture of the mountains above his desk.
assembled: fitted together to form a whole
The finished device was carefully assembled by hand in the factory.
observed: Unusual animal behaviour was observed just before the earthquake.
ever: Nobody can write down rules that nobody ever actually knew.
will: used to express the future tense
A fact heard once looks, from the inside, like a fact that will never be needed again.
exists: A structure that already exists is easier to fill than one built from nothing.
instead: He skipped dinner and had a light snack instead.
independent: free from outside control or influence
She moved out at eighteen to become more independent.
imperfect: not perfect; having faults or flaws
Even an imperfect plan is better than no plan at all.
different: not the same as another or each other
Every student in the class has a different learning style.
tested: checked or examined something to see how it performs
The new vaccine was tested on thousands of volunteers before approval.
against: in opposition to, or in contact with something
The team fought hard against the reigning champions.
instruments: plural of instrument: tools or devices, including musical ones
Surgeons sterilise their instruments before every operation.
coincide: to happen at the same time or place as something else
Her birthday happens to coincide with the national holiday this year.
everywhere: in, at, or to all places
It is controlled movement: letting the structure shift everywhere it needs to.
else: in addition to, or other than, someone or something already mentioned
Ask someone else if you need a second opinion on this.
weaker: That claim is a great deal weaker than saying the person came from that valley.
thing: an object, idea, or matter not named specifically
There's one thing I still don't understand about the plan.
misleading: giving a false or mistaken impression
The advertisement was criticised for being misleading about the product's benefits.
present: to show or offer something formally for others to consider
The scientist will present her findings at next week's conference.
otherwise: in a different way, or under different circumstances; if not
Wear a helmet; otherwise, you risk a serious head injury.
most: the majority of; the greatest amount or number of
Most of the guests had already left by the time the rain started.
human: relating to or characteristic of people

The robot cannot yet match human judgment in complex situations.
past: gone by in time; belonging to an earlier time
Over the past year, the company has doubled its workforce.
great: very large in size, amount, or degree
It takes a great deal of patience to learn a new language.
any: used to refer to one or some of a thing, no matter which
Do you have any questions before we begin the meeting?
science: the systematic study of the natural and physical world
Science has transformed our understanding of the universe.
knows: has information or understanding about something (he/she/it)
Nobody knows exactly when the tradition began.
times: plural of time; particular occasions or periods
This is why recipes that give exact times are unreliable.
attend: to be present at an event, or to witness something
Thousands of fans attended the concert despite the heavy rain.
